trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() for body-fragment, structure-aware text extraction. Every API call is documented in the rendered docs: create_fragment, next_tag, get_current_depth, next_token, get_token_type, and get_modifiable_text. The depth-bounded token walk and #text guard follow the documented subtree-text recipe, and the implementation naturally handles decoded entities, image-only empty text, no-H1 null, and unclosed H1 input. Functional result: 8/8, no _doing_it_wrong records.

Same reference-quality implementation. It uses the HTML Processor rather than the lexical Tag Processor, checks create_fragment() for null, finds only the first H1 opener, and walks the H1 subtree with get_current_depth() >= recorded depth. No undocumented methods or misuse. Functional result: 8/8, no _doing_it_wrong records.

Same correct documented pattern as trial 1. The #text-only accumulation avoids treating tags, comments, images, or special-element opener text as ordinary heading text, while get_modifiable_text() provides decoded text for #text nodes. Functional result: 8/8, no _doing_it_wrong records.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial. The docs did well in the exact places this task needed: the WP_HTML_Processor class overview says to use create_fragment() for BODY fragments and to choose the HTML Processor when document structure, element text, or subtree walking matters; the 'Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree' shows the same create_fragment + next_tag + get_current_depth + next_token + #text + get_modifiable_text pattern; next_token() explains that text requires token walking, that unclosed elements still produce structural closers, and that walks must be bounded by depth or breadcrumbs; get_current_depth() explicitly calls out the >= guard; get_modifiable_text() states that #text output is decoded UTF-8. The only near-miss is in the candidates' prose: they say get_modifiable_text() returns decoded text without restating the documented special cases for SCRIPT/STYLE/comments, but their code avoids that overreach by calling it only after get_token_type() === '#text'.

doc_gaps.problem: The subtree-walk pattern is documented well, but the cursor-position side effect at loop exit is easy to miss: the failing token, often the matched ancestor's closer or the first token outside the subtree, has already been consumed by next_token().
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short note to the depth-bounded walk examples explaining where the cursor is left after the loop and what callers should do if they need to continue scanning sibling regions.

doc_gaps.location: Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree
doc_gaps.problem: The recipe implies, but does not foreground, the result-policy distinction between 'no matching element' and 'matched element with no ordinary #text descendants'. That distinction is common for headings, links, cells, buttons, and image-only containers.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a generic sentence after the recipe: initialize the accumulator only after an element match; absence of the element is a caller-chosen sentinel, while a matched subtree with no #text tokens yields the empty string.

doc_gaps.problem: The method summary says it returns modifiable text, while the critical warning that it is not a predicate for ordinary DOM text appears later. Readers skimming method tables may still call it on every token.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Move a compact warning into the short description or method table summary: for DOM-style text extraction, first require get_token_type() === '#text'; comments and special-element tokens can also have modifiable text.
